system.storage.dataStorage.title: Payload Storage
system.storage.dataStorage.description: Where large request/response payloads (request bodies, response bodies, stream chunks) are stored. This does not change AxonHub's own database — it only offloads this bulky text content to a database, filesystem, or S3-compatible storage.

system.storage.policy.storeChunks.label: Store Response Chunks
system.storage.policy.storeChunks.descri: When enabled, raw stream chunks are saved to the default data storage (or the database when none is configured) after the stream ends, so you can replay them frame by frame in request details. A single streamed reply can produce hundreds of events — the highest storage cost. Keep off unless you need to debug streaming behavior.
system.storage.policy.livePreview.label: Live Preview
system.storage.policy.livePreview.descri: Show streaming output in real time on the request detail page while the request is still running. Memory only — nothing is saved, and it disappears when the request finishes or the server restarts.
system.storage.policy.storeRequestBody.d: Keep request debug copies for 5 minutes, up to 5 MiB each. Larger bodies are processed normally without a debug copy. Disabling this stops new request body storage.
Keep response debug copies for 5 minutes, up to 5 MiB each. When both body options are enabled, continuation context is retained separately for up to 2 hours. Disabling either option stops new disk continuation copies.
system.storage.policy.resourceTypeDescri: Clears stored request bodies and request headers only. Request rows and usage logs are kept.
Clears stored response bodies only. Request rows and usage logs are kept.
Clears stored response chunks only. Request rows and usage logs are kept.
system.storage.policy.cleanupDescription: Automatically remove old data after specified days to manage storage growth and comply with data retention policies. All related data of retained threads and traces will not be removed. Disable the toggle to keep data forever.
system.storage.policy.runCleanupError: Failed to start background cleanup task
system.storage.policy.runCleanupConfirmD: Are you sure you want to run cleanup now? This will permanently delete data according to policy (or all data if days is 0) and optimize the database.
system.storage.policy.runCleanupManualDe: Specify how many days back to clean up for each resource type. All related data of retained threads and traces will not be removed.
system.storage.policy.runCleanupPreviewE: No rows to delete and no payloads to clear.
system.storage.policy.runCleanupPreviewB: Only stored content is cleared. Rows with nothing left are skipped.
system.storage.policy.runCleanupPreviewF: Estimate timed out or failed. You can still run cleanup.

system.retry.title: Retry Policy
system.retry.description: Configure automatic retry behavior for failed requests to improve system reliability
system.retry.enabled.label: Enable Retry
system.retry.enabled.description: When enabled, the system will automatically retry failed requests. This helps improve reliability when experiencing temporary network issues or service unavailability.
system.retry.loadBalancerStrategy.label: Load Balancer Strategy
system.retry.loadBalancerStrategy.descri: Choose how channels are ordered when routing requests.
system.retry.loadBalancerStrategy.docume: Intelligently balances multiple factors including weight, success rate, and historical performance to select the optimal channel.
Orders channels by weight. Automatically switches to the next available channel upon failure.
Model Circuit Breaker. Tracks health per channel-model combination to isolate failures. Falls back to weight when a channel is healthy.
Rotates channels by historical request count so less-used channels are selected first. Channels with 3 recent consecutive failures are skipped behind healthy round-robin candidates.

Tracks circuit health per channel and upstream model. Within each model association priority, available channels are ordered by descending weight; historical performance breaks equal-weight ties. Sessions retain ownership only during the cache protection window and reselect after expiry. New sessions can immediately use a new higher-weight channel. If all combinations are broken, one last attempt is made; a counted failure returns 503.
system.retry.healthGate.title: Health gate
system.retry.healthGate.description: Circuit breaking is active only for health-gated routing. A failure threshold of 0 disables it globally.
system.retry.healthGate.ownerFailoverThr: Consecutive failovers before moving session ownership (K)
system.retry.healthGate.invalidValue: Enter a valid value: N may be 0; other fields must be positive, and durations must resolve to whole seconds.
system.retry.traceStickyMode.label: Session Affinity
system.retry.traceStickyMode.description: Prefer the most recently selected channel for the trace, then its thread. A failed sticky attempt falls back to normal channel ordering.
system.retry.maxChannelRetries.label: Max Channel Retries
system.retry.maxChannelRetries.descripti: Maximum number of times to retry across different channels (0-10). When a channel fails, the system will try other available channels up to this limit. Higher values increase reliability but may increase latency.
system.retry.maxSingleChannelRetries.des: Maximum number of times to retry on the same channel (0-10). Controls how many times to retry the same channel before switching to a different channel. Useful for temporary glitches.
system.retry.retryDelayMs.label: Retry Delay (ms)
system.retry.retryDelayMs.description: Delay between retry attempts in milliseconds (100-10000ms). Shorter delays provide faster recovery but may overwhelm struggling services. Longer delays give services more time to recover.
system.retry.streamFirstEventTimeoutSeco: Maximum seconds to wait for the first streaming event (0-600s). Set to 0 to disable.
system.retry.nonStreamResponseTimeoutSec: Maximum seconds to wait for a non-streaming response to complete (0-600s). Set to 0 to disable.
system.retry.emptyResponseDetection.desc: When enabled, the system pre-reads stream events to detect empty responses (no content generated). If detected, the empty response is treated as a failed attempt for subsequent retry handling.
system.retry.upstreamErrorPolicy.label: Upstream Error Display
system.retry.upstreamErrorPolicy.descrip: Control whether API users see raw provider errors. Request traces still keep the original error for administrators.
system.retry.upstreamErrorPolicy.customM: Enter the safe message returned to API users
system.retry.autoDisableChannel.label: Auto Disable Channel/API Key
system.retry.autoDisableChannel.descript: Automatically disable a channel or API key when consecutive errors match a rule. Inherit channels use these global rules; custom channels try their own rules first, then fall back here.
Webhook delivery is configured in the dedicated Webhook tab.
system.onboarding.title: System Onboarding
system.onboarding.description: Welcome to AxonHub! Let's set up your system with a quick tour.
system.onboarding.autoDisableChannel.des: A new feature has been added. Let's take a quick tour to understand how Auto Disable Channel works.
system.onboarding.steps.autoDisableIntro: You can define disable and recovery rules for consecutive errors. Inherit channels follow the global rules; a channel can add its own rules or turn auto-disable off.
system.onboarding.steps.autoDisableToggl: Turn on the switch, then add rules such as 401 × 3 → permanent disable or 429 × 3 → temporary disable for 30 minutes. Temporary and scheduled actions recover automatically; permanent disable stays until an operator re-enables it.
system.onboarding.steps.autoDisableCompl: Only a successful request clears consecutive counters. Keep thresholds reasonable (for example 3–5), and review inherit vs custom vs off on each channel.
system.onboarding.steps.welcome.title: Welcome to AxonHub!
system.onboarding.steps.welcome.descript: Let's configure your system settings to get started. This tour will guide you through setting up your brand, retry policies, and payload storage.
system.onboarding.steps.brandName.title: Set Your Brand Name
system.onboarding.steps.brandName.descri: Enter your organization or project name. This will be displayed throughout the interface.
system.onboarding.steps.brandLogo.title: Add Your Logo
system.onboarding.steps.brandLogo.descri: Upload your logo to customize the look and feel of AxonHub for your organization.
system.onboarding.steps.retryPolicy.desc: Set up automatic retry behavior for failed requests to improve reliability.
system.onboarding.steps.retryEnabled.des: Toggle retry functionality on or off. When enabled, failed requests will be automatically retried.
Set the maximum number of retry attempts for failed requests. Higher values increase reliability but may delay failure notifications.
system.onboarding.steps.retrySingleChann: Configure how many times to retry on the same channel before switching. Useful for temporary glitches.
system.onboarding.steps.retryDelay.title: Retry Delay
system.onboarding.steps.retryDelay.descr: Set the delay between retry attempts. Shorter delays provide faster recovery but may overwhelm struggling services.
system.onboarding.steps.dataStorage.desc: Configure how your data is stored and managed. This is important for performance and compliance.
system.onboarding.steps.storageEnabled.d: Choose what types of data to store. You can enable storage for chunks, request bodies, and response bodies.
system.onboarding.steps.storageChunks.de: Enable chunk storage for streaming responses. This allows you to view partial responses and analyze streaming behavior.
system.onboarding.steps.storageRequestBo: Save request payloads for debugging and analysis. This increases storage usage but provides valuable insights.
system.onboarding.steps.storageResponseB: Save response payloads for auditing and analysis. This significantly increases storage usage but provides complete data.
system.onboarding.steps.dataStorageSelec: Choose the storage backend for the request and response data. Different backends offer different performance and cost characteristics. Default is database, you can also configure other storage backends.
system.onboarding.steps.storageCleanupRe: Configure automatic cleanup for request data to manage storage space and maintain system performance.
system.onboarding.steps.storageCleanupUs: Set up cleanup policies for usage logs to comply with data retention requirements and optimize storage.
system.onboarding.steps.complete.title: Setup Complete!
system.onboarding.steps.complete.descrip: Great! Your system is now configured. You can always modify these settings later in the System Settings page.

system.maintenance.settings.diskPath: Disk path to monitor (empty for automatic)

system.maintenance.occupancyHint: These are current sizes of entire tables and indexes, including unexpired data, not space this cleanup will release. Payloads share tables with records; external file sizes are not included.
system.maintenance.tableSizesUnavailable: This database does not expose inexpensive per-table sizes. See the overview for total database size; preview does not scan all payloads.

system.transfer.title: Full deployment transfer
system.transfer.description: Export the full database, then validate and import it on a new deployment without business data. Existing JSON category transfers remain available below.
system.transfer.scope: Currently supports PostgreSQL → PostgreSQL. Includes database users, keys, channels, ledger, requests and statistics. External files and object storage must be transferred separately. The export contains sensitive configuration; store it securely.
system.transfer.fileLimit: File limit: {{size}}. Temporary files expire automatically.
system.transfer.uploadHint: Keep this page open during upload. Once uploaded and confirmed, the import continues in the background.
system.transfer.validating: Upload complete; waiting for server validation…
system.transfer.downloadStarted: Download handed to the browser. Check its download list for the result.
system.transfer.backgroundHint: The server continues this task after you leave. Return here for its latest status.
system.transfer.exportBytes: Written {{size}}. Final size is determined by the completed export.
system.transfer.restoreProgress: Restoring data, indexes and committing the transaction. Native restore does not expose an accurate overall percentage; the actual phase and continuously updated task status are shown.
system.transfer.switchSteps:
1. Change the destination deployment’s database name to {{database}} and restart it. Normal upgrade migrations run at startup.
2. Sign in using a source account and verify channels, keys, statistics and external storage.
3. Switch business traffic after verification. The current initialization database is unchanged.
system.transfer.failedDatabase: Interrupted or failed imports are not replayed automatically. Any new database is retained for inspection. Resolve that database before submitting a new import.
system.transfer.confirmDescription: Restore into a separate new database without overwriting the current database. Only for deployments that have not started serving business traffic.
system.transfer.trustedSource: Only import files you exported from a trusted AxonHub deployment. A checksum verifies integrity, not provenance. Native database archives can contain executable database code.
system.transfer.targetHint: Use a name that does not exist: letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore; up to 63 characters.
system.transfer.cutoverHint: Writes made after the export are not merged. For the final move, schedule a write-stop window and export the final snapshot. Verify external files, storage paths and connection settings separately.
system.transfer.confirmCheck: I trust the file source, this destination has no business traffic, and I understand the new database, space and switch requirements.
system.transfer.errors.unsupported: Full transfer requires PostgreSQL with a URL connection string. Existing JSON transfers remain available.
system.transfer.errors.tools_unavailable: Install pg_dump and pg_restore matching the PostgreSQL server major version.
system.transfer.errors.incompatible_vers: Client tools must match the server major version. Source application and PostgreSQL versions cannot exceed the destination.
system.transfer.errors.destination_not_e: This deployment already has business data. Full import is only available on a new destination.
system.transfer.errors.insufficient_spac: Insufficient free disk space; the task stopped. Free space while preserving the maintenance reserve.
system.transfer.errors.database_disk_una: Database disk capacity cannot be verified. Set database_transfer.database_disk_path to an accessible path on the actual database volume.
system.transfer.errors.invalid_package: Invalid package structure, size or checksum. Select a complete exported .axon.tar file.
system.transfer.errors.artifact_unavaila: Temporary file unavailable or expired. Multiple instances need a shared migration directory or sticky admin routing.
system.transfer.errors.submission_confli: Parameters changed for the same submission. Read the existing task status first.
system.transfer.errors.busy: Another transfer or download is running. Wait and read its status.
system.transfer.errors.migration_permiss: The database account needs permission to create databases and roles. See the transfer guide for restricted environments.
system.transfer.errors.target_database_e: Target database already exists or cannot be created. Use a valid new name.
system.transfer.errors.ownership_lost: Task ownership changed. Read its latest status.
system.transfer.errors.database_tool_fai: Database tool failed. Check client versions, connection and destination permissions. The task is not retried automatically.
system.transfer.errors.timeout: Task stopped at its configured time limit. Inspect the status and new database before proceeding.
system.transfer.errors.interrupted: Task interrupted and not replayed automatically. Read its status before proceeding.
system.transfer.errors.work_directory_un: Migration working directory unavailable. Check configuration and write permissions.
system.transfer.errors.operation_failed: Operation unsuccessful. Reload task status and check server configuration.
system.transfer.errors.status_unknown: Task result is currently unknown. Reload status; do not submit a duplicate import.
system.transfer.errors.upload_interrupte: Upload stopped. Reload server status, remove incomplete temporary files and upload again.
system.transfer.errors.file_too_large: File exceeds the configured limit. Check the package and server limit.
system.transfer.errors.owner_required: Only the system owner can perform full deployment transfers.
system.transfer.errors.confirmation_requ: Confirm the import scope and impact first.
system.webhook.events.providerQuotaWarni: Triggered when a provider channel enters the warning state, whether reported by the provider or derived from usage reaching the warning threshold.

system.retry.autoDisableChannel.noDelete: Global rules cannot delete credentials. Use permanent disable to keep the key for operators to inspect.
quota.label.period_quota_hint_provider: The whole window's worth and what it has consumed. The provider reports the window's money: its total is shown directly and the used amount is computed from the reported total and remainder.
quota.label.period_quota_hint_mixed: The whole window's worth and what it has consumed. When the provider reports the window's money, its total is shown directly and the used amount is computed from the reported total and remainder. Log-derived figures divide this channel's logged cost by the usage the provider reports, count only the usage AxonHub routed, and may be lower than the real quota.

system.quota.routing.modes.REMOVE_ON_EXH: Channels with exhausted quota are removed from routing until their quota resets. This is the default mode.
Channels burning quota faster than the window elapses keep serving only their existing sticky sessions; new sessions are routed to other available channels.

system.codex.permissions.channels: You need the "{{scope}}" permission to list, select, or test Codex channels.
system.codex.test.hint: The test uses the channel selected above even if it is not saved yet. It does not save settings, enable the channel, or depend on the switch above, and a failed test never blocks saving.
system.claudeCode.title: Auto-mode safeguards
system.claudeCode.description: Review tool calls from Claude Code requests that enable server-side safeguards. These settings do not control native Codex approval reviews.
system.claudeCode.serverDefaults: Using server configuration defaults. Saving creates a server-wide override that applies to new requests without a restart.
system.claudeCode.savedOverride: Using saved settings. Changes apply to new requests without a restart and override YAML/environment settings.
system.claudeCode.readOnly: You need write settings permission to make changes.
system.claudeCode.modelHelp: Leave blank to disable server-side review. Use a model ID or routing alias available through your channels. The calling API key and project must have access to every reviewer.
system.claudeCode.fallbackHelp: One model per line, or separated by commas. Tried in order when a review fails or is incomplete. Models must be distinct.
system.claudeCode.policyHelp: Nonempty text replaces the entire default decision policy, including any default rules you omit. Blank text uses the built-in policy. Evidence handling and verdict validation remain fixed.
system.claudeCode.escalateHelp: Allow a fallback reviewer to override a primary denial. If reassessment fails, the original denial is preserved.
system.claudeCode.limitsHelp: A per-reviewer timeout of 0 uses the remaining overall budget. Both timeouts are capped at 120 seconds. Output tokens: 1–16,384. Transcript bytes: 1–1,000,000.
system.claudeCode.saveFailed: Failed to save Claude Code safeguards settings
system.claudeCode.loadFailed: Failed to load Claude Code safeguards settings.
system.claudeCode.validation.fallbacks: Fallback models must be distinct and different from the reviewer model.
system.claudeCode.validation.limits: Enter valid timeouts, output token limits, and transcript limits.
